rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid equating cost with taste
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost of an article of furniture has at length come to be, with us, nearly the sole test of its merit in a decorative point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use mere parade of costly appurtenances as the test of beauty; avoid confusing magnificence (display of wealth) with true beauty or taste. Consider historical/social causes of 'show' (e.g., lack of aristocracy of blood) and resist parvenu rivalry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Room 'keeping' as an artistic principle
rubrics_metrics.description: We speak of the keeping of a room as we would of the keeping of a picture—for both the picture and the room are amenable to those undeviating principles which regulate all varieties of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess rooms by the same principles used for paintings: unified effect, coherence, restraint. 'Keeping' includes arrangement, harmony of colors, and suitability of each piece to the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overuse of straight lines and harsh right angles
rubrics_metrics.description: Straight lines are too prevalent—too uninterruptedly continued—or clumsily interrupted at right angles. If curved lines occur, they are repeated into unpleasant uniformity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent visual monotony from too many uninterrupted straight lines or repeated identical curves; seek balanced, varied line work and avoid undue precision that spoils effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curtain proportion and compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: With formal furniture, curtains are out of place; and an extensive volume of drapery of any kind is, under any circumstance, irreconcilable with good taste—the proper quantum, as well as the proper adjustment, depending upon the character of the general effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose curtain style and amount to match the furniture and overall character of the room; avoid excessive drapery and use restraint in volume and adjustment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carpet as the soul of the apartment
rubrics_metrics.description: The soul of the apartment is the carpet. From it are deduced not only the hues but the forms of all objects incumbent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select carpet pattern and texture carefully: a large floor may have large figures, a small one small figures. Prefer Saxony texture; avoid Brussels and Turkey (deprecated). Use distinct grounds and vivid circular or cycloid figures; avoid pictorial or floral representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pictorial/flower patterns in upholstery
rubrics_metrics.description: The abomination of flowers, or representations of well-known objects of any kind, should not be endured within the limits of Christendom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer arabesque and abstract ornament rather than representational motifs on carpets, curtains, tapestry, or ottoman coverings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject 'glare'—avoid gas and unshaded glass indoors
rubrics_metrics.description: Glare is a leading error ... We are violently enamoured of gas and of glass. The former is totally inadmissible within doors. Its harsh and unsteady light offends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use mild or 'cool' light with warm shadows; avoid gas and cut-glass shades. The Argand lamp with a plain ground-glass shade is recommended for tempered uniform illumination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid cut-glass shades and flashiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The cut-glass shade is a weak invention ... The eagerness with which we have adopted it, partly on account of its 'flashiness', but principally on account of its 'greater rest', is a good commentary on the proposition with which we began.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not employ cut-glass shades; their broken, unequal light is unpleasant and can mar the appearance of even good furniture and female loveliness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid enormous, unshaded, glittering chandeliers
rubrics_metrics.description: The huge and unmeaning glass chandeliers, prism-cut, gas-lighted, and without shade, which dangle in our most fashionable drawing-rooms, may be cited as the quintessence of all that is false in taste or preposterous in folly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eschew large prism-cut, unshaded chandeliers that produce harsh, flickering lights; prefer steady, tempered lighting sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit the use of mirrors
rubrics_metrics.description: The rage for 'glitter' ... has led us, also, to the exaggerated employment of mirrors. ... the mirror presents a continuous, flat, colourless, unrelieved surface ... a room with four or five mirrors arranged at random, is, for all purposes of artistic show, a room of no shape at all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid numerous or very large mirrors; if used, limit to a single, modest-sized mirror placed so as not to reflect ordinary sitting-places. Too many mirrors create uniformity and disorder the room's shape.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer few large paintings and restrained frames
rubrics_metrics.description: Not one is of small size. Diminutive paintings give that 'spotty' look to a room, which is the blemish of so many a fine work of Art overtouched. The frames are broad but not deep, and richly carved, without being dulled or filagreed. They lie flat on the walls, and do not hang off with cords.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor several substantial paintings of warm but dark tone; avoid many small pictures; use broad shallow frames, hung flat rather than with cords to prevent a spotty appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal extraneous furniture and covers
rubrics_metrics.description: Beyond these things, there is no furniture, if we except an Argand lamp ... This is also without cover—the drapery of the curtains has been thought sufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid overcovering tables/pianos and overfurnishing; allow curtain drapery to suffice instead of additional covers; keep the room uncluttered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color and textile coordination determine room character
rubrics_metrics.description: The colours of the curtains and their fringe—the tints of crimson and gold—appear everywhere in profusion, and determine the 'character' of the room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let predominant textiles (curtains, carpet) set the palette and mood; coordinate other elements to support the main color scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carpet texture preference: Saxony recommended
rubrics_metrics.description: As regards texture, the Saxony is alone admissible. Brussels is the preterpluperfect tense of fashion, and Turkey is taste in its dying agonies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose Saxony texture for carpet; avoid Brussels and Turkish rugs if aiming for timeless good taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid ostentatious or incoherent patterned floor-cloths
rubrics_metrics.description: Those antique floor-cloth ... cloths of huge, sprawling, and radiating devises, stripe-interspersed, and glorious with all hues, among which no ground is intelligible—these are but the wicked invention of a race of time-servers and money-lovers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reject overcrowded, radiating, kaleidoscopic floor patterns that create incoherence; prefer intelligible grounds and measured ornament.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use lighting to create warm shadows and repose
rubrics_metrics.description: A mild, or what artists term a cool light, with its consequent warm shadows, will do wonders for even an ill-furnished apartment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design lighting to produce calm, shadowed effects that flatter furnishings and occupants rather than harsh illumination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid flashy glitter in glass and ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: Its leading feature is glitter—and in that one word how much of all that is detestable do we express! Flickering, unquiet lights, are sometimes pleasing—to children and idiots always so—but in the embellishment of a room they should be scrupulously avoided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steer clear of glittery, flickering ornamentation—these appeal to low tastes and harm refined decorative effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not hang pictures off the wall with cords
rubrics_metrics.description: They lie flat on the walls, and do not hang off with cords. The designs themselves are often seen to better advantage in this latter position, but the general appearance of the chamber is injured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hang frames flat against the wall rather than suspended by cords to maintain unified wall plane and room 'keeping'.
